extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, and examiners handling sequence listings, computer program listing appendices, and read-only optical disc submissions to the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for preparing and submitting Sequence Listings (including Sequence Listing XML), Computer Program Listing Appendices, Large Tables, and related files via the USPTO Patent Electronic Filing System or on read-only optical disc. Covers file formats, labeling, transmittal content, amendment procedures, and examiner form paragraphs for common defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-filing submission of Sequence Listing XML - required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a “Sequence Listing XML” after the filing date requires that the applicant provide: (1) a request to amend the specification to include an updated incorporation by reference statement of the material in the “Sequence Listing XML” (37 CFR 1.835(a)(2)); (2) a statement that identifies the basis for the amendment with specific references to particular parts of the application as originally filed (specification, claims, drawings) for all sequence data in the “Sequence Listing XML” in the application as originally filed (37 CFR 1.835(a)(3)); and (3) a statement of no new matter (37 CFR 1.835(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must explicitly request amendment to include incorporation-by-reference paragraph, cite exact basis in originally filed materials for all sequence data, and affirm no new matter. These three elements are required for any Sequence Listing XML submitted after the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement Sequence Listing XML - required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a replacement “Sequence Listing XML” (e.g., after notice of an error), applicant must submit: (1) a request to amend the specification to include an incorporation by reference statement of the material in the replacement “Sequence Listing XML” (37 CFR 1.835(b)(2)); (2) a statement that identifies the location of all additions, deletions, or replacements of sequence information relative to the replaced file (37 CFR 1.835(b)(3)); (3) a statement that identifies the basis for the additions, deletions, or replacements with specific references to parts of the originally filed application for all amended sequence data (37 CFR 1.835(b)(4)); and (4) a statement of no new matter (37 CFR 1.835(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement XML must (a) request incorporation-by-reference to the replacement file, (b) enumerate and locate all changes relative to the prior submission, (c) provide the basis in the originally filed application for any amended sequence data, and (d) state no new matter. These items map to specific CFR sections and are required for replacement submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size limit for Sequence Listing XML files
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred (100) megabytes is the size limit for a “Sequence Listing XML” submitted as an XML file via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure XML files uploaded to EFS do not exceed 100 MB. If larger, must be split/compressed in accordance with applicable rules (see 37 CFR provisions referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc media and ISO standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A read-only optical disc submitted under 37 CFR 1.52(e) is a finalized disc, in conformance with International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9660, on which the data is recorded so it is permanent and cannot be changed or erased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted media: CD-ROM, CD-R, DVD-R, DVD+R. Erasable/rewriteable media (CD-RW, DVD-RW, DVD+RW) are not acceptable. Discs must be finalized to ISO 9660 to ensure permanence and longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format requirements for contents of read-only optical disc
rubrics_metrics.description: For 'Large Tables,' a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix,' a 'Sequence Listing,' or a CRF of a 'Sequence Listing,' the contents of each read-only optical disc must be in ASCII plain text file format. For a 'Sequence Listing XML,' the contents of each read-only optical disc must be in XML file format and must be encoded using Unicode UTF-8. All permitted printable and control characters are defined by WIPO ST.26. Each text file must have a .txt extension; each XML file must have a .xml extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No non-ASCII characters or proprietary file formats are permitted for ASCII submissions. Use a text viewer to verify ASCII. For XML, use UTF-8 encoding and conform to ST.26 character set. Ensure correct file extensions and avoid proprietary formats (e.g., Word/Excel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of unreadable or non-compliant files on disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Material on a read-only optical disc is generally treated as part of the originally filed disclosure when filed on the application filing date, but if a file is unreadable or fails to comply with the requirements (e.g., wrong format), it is treated as not having been submitted and will not be part of the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify readability and compliance before submission; the Office will check for readability and format and will issue notices if files are unreadable. Unreadable or non-compliant files may require resubmission; they are treated as never submitted for filing-date purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility requirements for read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must be compatible with PC or Mac® computers and with MS-DOS®, MS-Windows®, Mac OS®, or Unix®/Linux® operating systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common cross-platform formats, avoid proprietary OS-specific encodings, and test discs on representative systems to confirm compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter contents for read-only optical disc submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(e)(4) requires that each read-only optical disc must be enclosed in a hard case within an unsealed padded and protective mailing envelope and accompanied by a transmittal letter. The transmittal letter must include: 1) first-named inventor (if known); 2) title of the invention; 3) attorney docket or file reference number (if applicable); 4) application number and filing date (if known); 5) the operating system used to produce the disc; and 6) the files contained on the disc, including the name of the file, the size of the file in bytes, and the date of creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting any of the required transmittal information will trigger an examiner objection (form paragraphs provided). Ensure the transmittal letter lists each disc's files and required metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirements for read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must have a permanent label affixed thereto on which the following information has been hand-printed or typed: 1) first-named inventor (if known); 2) title of the invention; 3) attorney docket or file reference number (if applicable); 4) application number and filing date (if known); 5) date on which the data were recorded on the read-only optical disc; and 6) disc order (e.g., '1 of X') if multiple discs are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels must be permanent and clearly identify disc order when multiple discs are used. Failure to label correctly will trigger objections and processing problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication and return policy for read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Read-only optical discs submitted to the Office will not be returned to the applicant and may not be retained as part of the patent application file. Read-only optical discs containing 'Large Tables' or a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' must be submitted in duplicate and labeled as 'Copy 1' and 'Copy 2.' 'Sequence Listing' discs and 'Sequence Listing XML' discs are not required to be submitted in duplicate because they are processed differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit duplicate discs when required (Large Tables, Computer Program Listing Appendix). Office will retain one copy or process per stated procedures; applicants should keep their own backups because discs are not returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing, checks, and processing of read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Read-only optical discs containing 'Large Tables' and/or a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' should be routed to OPAP, while discs containing a 'Sequence Listing', a CRF of a 'Sequence Listing', or a 'Sequence Listing XML' should be routed to PLRC. Discs will be checked for viruses, readability, the presence of non-ASCII or non-XML files, and compliance with file and disc labeling requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will perform virus/readability/format checks. If defects are found (e.g., unreadable file, virus), OPAP or PLRC will issue notices and require replacement submissions per applicable CFRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to read-only optical disc content — replacement-only rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the information on a read-only optical disc must be by way of a replacement read-only optical disc, in compliance with 37 CFR 1.58(g) for 'Large Tables', 37 CFR 1.96(c)(5) for a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix', 37 CFR 1.825(b) for a 'Sequence Listing' or CRF, and 37 CFR 1.835(b) for a 'Sequence Listing XML'. Replacement discs must include all files of the original disc that were not amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot edit disc contents via the electronic filing system to change a previously submitted disc; file a complete replacement disc containing all unamended and amended files. Missing unamended files on a replacement will trigger an objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and common defects for read-only disc submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides numerous examiner form paragraphs to notify applicants of common defects: e.g., ¶6.60.01 (no statement that duplicate discs are identical), ¶6.60.02 (transmittal letter missing listing), ¶6.61.01 (specification lacking list of discs/files), ¶6.61.02 (missing incorporation by reference statement), ¶6.62 (data file not ASCII/XML), ¶6.72.03 (discs not readable), ¶6.72.04 (disc contains viruses), ¶6.72.01 (duplicate discs not identical), ¶6.72.05 (missing files on amended disc), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cited form paragraphs to understand examiner objections and required corrections. Many objections require resubmission of properly formatted files, insertion or amendment of incorporation-by-reference statements, or replacement discs labeled correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix — thresholds and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 37 CFR 1.96: a computer program listing of 300 lines or fewer (each line ≤72 characters) may be submitted either as drawings or as part of the specification. Any listing having more than 60 lines submitted as part of the specification must be positioned at the end of the description but before the claims; listings of 301 lines or more must be submitted as an electronic ASCII plain text file (Computer Program Listing Appendix) via EFS or on a read-only optical disc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If listing ≤300 lines you may include in spec or as drawings; if >300 lines must be electronic appendix. If included in the spec and >60 lines, place at end before claims. Follow substitution-sheet rules for amendments to in-spec listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix — file content and compatibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' must conform to: (i) computer compatibility: PC or Mac; (ii) operating system compatibility: MS–DOS, MS-Windows, Mac OS, or Unix/Linux; (iii) line terminator: ASCII CRLF or LF only; and (iv) control codes: data must not depend on control characters or codes not defined in the ASCII character set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure listings use only ASCII characters and line terminators CRLF or LF; avoid platform-specific control codes. Test files on target OS environments to confirm compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix — file naming and size constraints (EFS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each file must be named as *.txt where '*' is limited to letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores, contains no spaces or other characters, and does not exceed 60 characters excluding the extension. Each file submitted via EFS must not exceed 25 MB, and file compression is not permitted for EFS submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose concise filenames with allowed characters and ≤60 characters. For EFS uploads, keep file sizes ≤25 MB and do not compress. Use multiple files or read-only disc submission if size exceeds limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix — read-only optical disc-specific rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitted in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e): (i) a separate read-only optical disc containing a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' must be submitted for each application; (ii) multiple program listings for a single application may be placed on a single disc; (iii) multiple read-only discs may be submitted if necessary; (iv) listings may be compressed into a single file using WinZip, 7-Zip, or Unix/Linux Zip; (v) compressed files must not be self-extracting; and (vi) a compressed ASCII plain text file that does not fit on a single disc may be split into multiple file parts, labeled in compliance with disc labeling rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using discs, compression (zip) is permitted but avoid self-extracting archives. If splitting across discs, label file parts and discs clearly per §1.52(e)(5)(vi) so Office can reassemble. Submit duplicate discs for Computer Program Listing Appendix (Copy 1/Copy 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Computer Program Listing Appendix — replacement and required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendments to a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' in electronic ASCII plain text form must include: (i) a replacement ASCII plain text file submitted via EFS or on a read-only optical disc (replacement discs submitted in duplicate and labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'); (ii) a request that the amendment be made by incorporation by reference of the material in the replacement file in a separate paragraph of the specification identifying the name, date of creation, and size in bytes (§1.77(b)(5)); (iii) a statement identifying the location of all deletions, replacements, or additions to the ASCII file; and (iv) a statement that the replacement ASCII plain text file contains no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement submission must be a full-file replacement and include explicit incorporation-by-reference amendment language in the specification plus change-location and no-new-matter statements. Follow labeling conventions for replacement discs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification incorporation-by-reference requirement for Computer Program Listing Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification of a complete application with a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' filed on the application filing date, without an incorporation by reference of the material contained in the ASCII plain text file, must be amended to contain a separate paragraph incorporating by reference the material in accordance with §1.77(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you file an ASCII program listing on the filing date, immediately include an incorporation-by-reference paragraph in the specification identifying the file name, date, and size. Examiners will require insertion if omitted.
